days.title: Leave Cairo
days.summary: Night flight: EgyptAir nonstop to Tokyo Narita at 11:45 pm.

items.title: Leave for Cairo Airport, Terminal 3
items.note: Be at Terminal 3 by about 8:45 pm, 3 hours before the flight. EgyptAir includes two checked bags of 23 kg and one 8 kg cabin bag each on this fare. Carry the passports with the Japan visa, the hotel bookings and the printed return ticket: Japanese immigration can ask for them.
items.stepsWhy: Check-in, security and the walk to the gate at Cairo airport

items.title: EgyptAir MS964, nonstop: Cairo → Tokyo Narita
items.note: 11 h 45 min nonstop, landing at 6:30 pm on Fri 4 Dec (Tokyo is 7 hours ahead of Cairo). Sleep as much as you can: you land in the evening. Already counted under Flights & visa.
items.stepsWhy: Aisle walks on a 12-hour flight

days.title: Arrive in Tokyo
days.summary: Land at Narita at 6:30 pm, Narita Express to Tokyo Station, check in at lyf Ginza and a late dinner nearby.

items.title: Land at Narita Terminal 1: immigration, bags and train tickets
items.note: Fill in Visit Japan Web on the phone before landing: it gives the QR codes for immigration and customs. In the arrivals hall, buy the Narita Express round-trip ticket for foreign visitors at the JR East Travel Service Center or the ticket machines (passport needed), and a Welcome Suica card each for metro rides (top up ¥3,000 each to start).
items.stepsWhy: Gate to immigration, bags and the walk to the station under Terminal 1

items.title: Narita Express to Tokyo Station
items.place: Narita Express (N'EX)

items.note: About 55–60 min to Tokyo Station, reserved seats, luggage racks at the car ends. Trains run about every 30–60 min in the evening: take the first one after you clear customs. The round-trip ticket covers the ride back to Narita on 11 Dec (valid 14 days).
items.stepsWhy: Seated on the train

items.title: Dinner: vegan ramen at T's Tantan, Tokyo Station
items.place: T's Tantan (Gransta Tokyo), Gransta Tokyo B1F (Square Zero area), JR Tokyo Station, 1-9-1 Marunouchi, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo 100-0005
items.cuisine: Vegan ramen (sesame tantanmen, yuzu salt ramen, vegan gyoza)
items.halalSource: Fully vegan ramen shop (no meat, fish, egg or dairy). Beer is sold (Heartland ¥800). No pork or meat anywhere on the menu. (https://ts-restaurant.jp/tantan/)
items.hours: Fri 10:00 am - 10:00 pm (last order 9:30 pm)
items.note: Keep the suitcases at the table if there is room, or use the large coin lockers next to Gransta (about ¥700–900). Order: Japanese Yuzu Sio (salt) Ramen ¥1,250 for a light bowl, or Golden Sesame Tantanmen ¥1,250 (not marked hot); skip the black sesame (hot) version; 3 or 6 gyoza to share. The shop moved on 1 Aug 2026 from Keiyo Street (inside the gates) to Gransta Tokyo B1F, outside the gates; older guides still give the old spot. Last order is 9:30 pm, so they must be in the queue by about 9:15 pm; arriving at Tokyo Station at 8:15 pm leaves enough time, but with only about 12 seats a Friday queue is possible. If the line is long, Soranoiro Nippon (Tokyo Ramen Street, same basement) is open until 10:30 pm. Inside the station basement, so no outdoor walk with luggage before dinner;
items.costBasis: ¥1,650 each: Japanese yuzu salt ramen or golden sesame tantanmen ¥1,250 + 3 vegan gyoza ¥400 (Oct 2026 menu)
items.rating: HappyCow 5.0 (1,071 reviews); Google and Tabelog not found
items.stepsWhy: About 4 min from the Narita Express platform to Gransta B1F

alts.title: Dinner: vegan ramen at Soranoiro, Tokyo Ramen Street
alts.place: Soranoiro Nippon (Tokyo Ramen Street), Tokyo Ramen Street, Tokyo Station Ichibangai B1F, unit R-2, 1-9-1 Marunouchi, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo 100-0005
alts.cuisine: Ramen with a vegan menu (vegan ramen, vegan tantanmen, vegan gyoza)
alts.halalSource: Only the vegan bowls qualify; the shop also sells non-vegan ramen. Past reviewers said a 'vegetarian' broth contained shellfish or butter, so order an item labelled vegan. Alcohol not confirmed. (https://www.happycow.net/reviews/soranoiro-tokyo-120511)
alts.hours: Fri 9:00 am - 10:30 pm (one older source says 9:00 am - 11:00 pm, last order 10:30 pm)
alts.note: Order: The vegan shio (salt) or shoyu ramen; ask staff to confirm it is the vegan broth. Later closing than T's Tantan, which makes it the fallback if they arrive late or the T's Tantan queue is long. Some reviewers found the vegan ramen less tasty than other vegan ramen in Tokyo. Tokyo Ramen Street is in the Yaesu-side basement, so the walk on to the hotel, lyf Ginza Tokyo (2-5-4 Kyobashi), is about 8-10 minutes via the Yaesu exit. Do not confuse it with the Soranoiro branch in Kyobashi, which serves pork tonkotsu ramen.
alts.costBasis: ¥1,400 each: one vegan ramen bowl (exact 2026 price not confirmed)
alts.stepsWhy: About 1 min closer each way than the planned meal

items.title: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Street, Asakusa

move.route: Walk 2 min to Kyobashi station, Ginza line to Asakusa (about 17 min), then the Kaminarimon gate is next to exit 1.
move.source: fare from the operator's fare table (IC card fare)

items.note: Tokyo's oldest temple, free. The grounds are always open; the main hall 6:00 am – 5:00 pm. Walk in through the Kaminarimon gate and its giant lantern, then Nakamise Street (souvenir and snack stalls, open about 10:00 am), the five-storey pagoda and the main hall. Saturday mornings get busy after 10:30 am.
items.stepsWhy: Station corridors, then about 2 h walking the temple grounds, Nakamise and the side streets

items.cuisine: Halal wagyu ramen and gyukatsu (wagyu beef cutlet)

items.note: Order: White Broth A5 Wagyu Ramen (or Clear Broth Chicken Ramen for the lightest bowl); share one A5 wagyu cutlet set if hungry; skip the spicy and fried-chicken ramen. One reviewer called it a bit pricey, another good value. The gyukatsu (fried wagyu cutlet) is the 'rough' option; the ramen is the easy one.

items.title: Meiji Jingu shrine

move.route: Ginza line from Asakusa to Omotesando (about 30 min), Chiyoda line one stop to Meiji-jingumae (Harajuku), then the shrine gate is next to the station.
move.source: fare from the operator's fare table (IC card fare)

items.note: Free. The shrine to Emperor Meiji in a forest in the middle of the city: a 10 min walk on gravel under huge torii gates to the main hall. In December the gates open at 6:40 am and close at 4:00 pm (sunset), so go by about 3:00 pm.
items.stepsWhy: Gravel forest path about 10 min each way, plus the shrine courtyard

items.title: Takeshita Street, Harajuku

move.route: From the shrine gate across the road to Takeshita Street.

items.note: Optional: the narrow street of crêpe stands, fashion and character shops, very crowded on Saturdays. Omotesando avenue next to it has the big brands.
items.stepsWhy: Optional: about 30 min along the street

items.title: Shibuya Sky at sunset

move.route: JR Yamanote line from Harajuku to Shibuya (2 min), then follow the signs to Shibuya Scramble Square; the ticket floor is the 14th.

items.note: Book the 3:40 pm or 4:00 pm entry slot: sunset is about 4:28 pm, and you stay on the open-air roof as the city lights come on. Bags go in free lockers before the roof; hats and loose items are not allowed up there. Dress warmly: it is windy at 229 m.
items.stepsWhy: Lifts, then about an hour walking around the open roof deck

items.title: Shibuya Crossing and the Hachiko statue

items.note: Free. Cross the scramble a couple of times, then look down on it from the second-floor windows of the Shibuya station passage (the Mark City walkway) or the MAGNET building's rooftop.
items.stepsWhy: About 30 min crossing and walking around the square

Use the Tokyo Disney Resort app for waiting times; Disney Premier Access (paid in the app on the day): Anna and Elsa's Frozen Journey and Soaring ¥2,500 each, Peter Pan and Toy Story Mania! ¥2,000. If you pick Disneyland instead: Christmas parade 12:45 pm, Electrical Parade Dreamlights 7:00 pm, fireworks 8:30 pm. visas.title: Short-term tourist visa, single entry
visas.costLabel: 10,000 EGP for two, cash on collection
visas.summary: Needed: Egyptians living in Egypt cannot use Japan's eVISA. Apply in person at the Embassy of Japan in Maadi; the embassy keeps the passports while it processes (at least 5 working days, not guaranteed; it advises 3 weeks ahead). As plan B this is the hard part: the China visa hand-in (22–26 Nov) also needs the passports, and waiting for the China result first leaves too little time for a 3 Dec departure.
facts: 5,000 EGP (about US$93), paid in cash when you collect the visa. Multiple entry 10,000 EGP.

Minimum 5 business days, not guaranteed; may take longer depending on the case. The embassy strongly advises applying at least 3 weeks before departure. Results are announced by uploading the acceptance number on the embassy website.

High risk. Counting embassy working days (Sun - Thu): submitting Sun 22 Nov or Mon 23 Nov gives the earliest result around Mon 30 Nov - Tue 1 Dec; submitting Tue 24 Nov -> around Tue 1 Dec; Wed 25 Nov -> Wed 2 Dec; Thu 26 Nov -> Thu 3 Dec, the departure day. The 5 days are a minimum, not a promise, and any request for extra documents adds days. The embassy keeps the passports while processing, so flights and hotels booked now could be lost if the visa is late. Prefer refundable flights/hotels, submit on Sun 22 Nov if possible with a complete file (stamped English bank statements, employment letters, marriage certificate translation), and keep travel insurance in mind.

In person at the Consular Section, Embassy of Japan, 1st floor, 81 Corniche El Nil Street, Maadi, Cairo. No appointment needed for application or pickup. Sunday - Thursday 9:00 am - 2:00 pm (be at the gate at least 20 minutes before closing; security check). Closed Friday, Saturday and embassy holidays. No embassy holidays fall between 22 Nov and 3 Dec 2026 (next: 30 - 31 Dec). Documents cannot be sent by mail, fax or email. No designated agencies are mentioned; Egyptian citizens apply directly at the embassy.
A single-entry visa is valid for entry within 3 months from the date of issue.
Fill in Visit Japan Web before landing for the immigration and customs QR codes.
documents: Visa application form, filled in and signed (one per person)
1 recent passport-size photo, white background (damaged or old photos refused)
Certificate of employment showing salary, tenure and position (enrollment certificate for students)
Original stamped bank statement for the last 3 months, in English
If applying together as a family: proof of relationship (e.g. marriage certificate)
All Arabic documents need an English or Japanese translation attached; attach a copy of the flight, hotel and itinerary to each application; do not staple. Additional documents may be requested.
